q: A technician suspects a Windows workstation is infected with malware. As part of the standard malware removal process, which action should be performed BEFORE running a full anti-malware scan?
options: Disable System Restore and boot into Safe Mode
Enable AutoRun on all removable drives to test infection vectors
Connect the machine to a different network segment and ignore the scan
explanation: Disabling System Restore prevents malware from hiding in restore points. Booting into Safe Mode prevents many malware processes from loading, allowing the scanner to detect and remove them more effectively.

q: After removing malware from a workstation, which two actions are MOST important before returning the machine to the user?
options: Disable Windows Update and remove the antivirus to improve performance
Re-enable System Restore and lower the UAC level to reduce prompts
Update anti-malware definitions and apply all outstanding OS patches
Schedule a scan for six months in the future and clear the event logs
explanation: Updating anti-malware definitions ensures protection against the latest threats, and applying OS patches closes vulnerabilities the malware may have exploited. These are core steps in the remediation and prevention phase.

q: A user's workstation shows signs of infection: changed browser homepage, constant pop-ups, and degraded performance. The technician quarantines the machine. What does quarantining accomplish?
options: It permanently deletes all infected files from the hard drive
It encrypts infected files using BitLocker to prevent further spread
It re-images the workstation from a known-good baseline
It isolates suspected malware files so they cannot execute while preserving them for analysis
explanation: Quarantine moves suspected malware to an isolated location where it cannot execute or spread, while preserving it for analysis or vendor submission. Deletion is irreversible and may be premature before confirmation.

q: What is the FIRST security action to take when setting up a new workstation?

q: What type of software should be kept updated to ensure it can detect the latest malware?

q: What is the purpose of a host-based firewall such as Windows Firewall?
options: Filter incoming and outgoing traffic on the individual computer

Disable or delete the account immediately
Change the password and share it with the team

options: Only allow autorun for trusted brands
Disable autorun/autoplay to prevent automatic execution of potentially malicious code

q: A company policy requires workstations to automatically lock after inactivity and require re-authentication. Which Windows feature enforces this?
explanation: The screen saver timeout combined with "On resume, display logon screen" (enforced via Group Policy) is the standard Windows mechanism for automatic workstation locking after inactivity.

q: A technician is hardening a new Windows workstation. Which action BEST demonstrates applying the principle of least privilege?
options: Creating a separate administrator account for administrative tasks and using a standard account for daily use
Granting the standard user account local administrator rights to simplify software installs
Disabling Windows Defender to allow all applications to run without restrictions
Configuring the firewall to allow all outbound traffic by default
explanation: Using a standard account for daily tasks and a separate administrator account only when needed limits the damage any malware or mistake can cause, implementing least privilege at the user level.

q: A technician wants to prevent users from running unauthorized applications on company workstations without blocking the entire OS. Which Windows Enterprise feature allows application whitelisting?
explanation: AppLocker allows administrators to define rules permitting or denying specific applications, scripts, and installer files based on file path, publisher signature, or hash. It is the primary application whitelisting tool in Windows Enterprise and Education editions.

q: What mobile security feature wipes the device after a specified number of failed unlock attempts?
options: Failed login wipe or remote wipe after threshold

q: What MDM capability allows an IT admin to lock or wipe a lost corporate mobile device remotely?

options: Bring Your Own Device — concern is mixing personal and corporate data on unmanaged devices
Buy Your Own Device — concern is cost
Build Your Own Device — concern is compatibility
Backup Your Own Data — concern is compliance

q: What type of screen lock is considered the most secure on mobile devices?
options: Strong alphanumeric passcode or biometric with backup passcode

q: What security feature on mobile devices verifies each app is from a trusted source before installation?
options: App signing and app store vetting (e.g., Play Protect, App Store review)

q: A company issues smartphones to employees and requires that all corporate data be erasable from any device reported lost or stolen. Which mobile device management capability satisfies this?
explanation: Remote wipe allows an administrator via MDM to send a command that erases all data on the device over the network. GPS helps locate a device but does not protect data on it.

q: An employee enrolls their personal smartphone in the company MDM solution for BYOD access to corporate resources. Which security concern does MDM enrollment PRIMARILY address?
options: Enforcing security policies such as screen lock, encryption, and remote wipe on the personal device
Preventing the employee from making personal calls during work hours
Blocking all personal app installations on the employee's device
Automatically upgrading device hardware to meet corporate standards
explanation: MDM enrollment allows IT to enforce baseline security policies on personal devices accessing corporate resources, balancing employee privacy with corporate data protection requirements.

q: The IT department wants to ensure that if the physical storage chip is removed from a corporate smartphone, stored data cannot be read by an attacker. Which feature provides this protection?
explanation: Full device encryption encrypts all data on internal storage using a key derived from the user's PIN or password. Without the decryption key, data removed on physical media is unreadable.

q: A mobile device requires a fingerprint scan to unlock. If the fingerprint reader fails, it falls back to a numeric PIN. Which security concept does this configuration illustrate?
options: Multi-factor authentication with a fallback method
Remote wipe triggered by failed biometric attempts
explanation: The fingerprint (something you are) and PIN (something you know) represent two authentication factors. The fallback ensures usability when biometrics fail, though the fallback alone is single-factor.

q: An organization's mobile device policy requires all apps on corporate devices to be vetted before installation. Which MDM mechanism enforces this on managed devices?
options: Corporate app catalog / MDM application whitelist
explanation: MDM solutions can restrict app installation to an approved corporate catalog, blocking public app stores or sideloaded packages, ensuring all applications have been reviewed for security and compliance.

q: What data sanitization method overwrites all data on a drive multiple times with random patterns?
What method destroys magnetic media data by exposing it to a powerful magnetic field?
Which disposal method is the MOST secure for ensuring data on a hard drive is unrecoverable?
Which regulatory standard governs the secure disposal of healthcare patient data in the United States?
A government contractor must dispose of hard drives containing classified data and provide a written record of destruction. Which combination satisfies BOTH requirements?
options: Physical shredding or incineration plus a certificate of destruction
Standard format and delete, with a deletion log saved to a network share
Overwriting once with zeros and recycling the drives
Removing the drives and storing them in a locked cabinet
explanation: Physical destruction ensures data is unrecoverable by eliminating the storage medium entirely. A certificate of destruction is an auditable document confirming the method and date, satisfying documentation requirements for regulated environments.

q: A technician must sanitize spinning hard drives being donated to a school so data is removed but drives remain functional. Which method is MOST appropriate?
options: Multi-pass overwrite using a DoD 5220.22-M compliant tool
Deleting all files and emptying the Recycle Bin
explanation: A multi-pass overwrite (e.g., DoD 5220.22-M) renders data unrecoverable on spinning magnetic drives while leaving the drive functional for reuse. Shredding destroys the drive; deleting files does not sanitize the disk.

q: Which data sanitization method exposes magnetic storage media to a powerful magnetic field, randomizing all stored data and rendering the drive inoperable?
explanation: Degaussing uses a strong magnetic field to randomize the magnetic domains on a drive or tape, destroying all data. Because it damages servo tracks and firmware, the drive is non-functional afterward and cannot be reused.

q: According to NIST SP 800-88, which sanitization category describes making data unrecoverable by any known technique, typically through physical destruction?
explanation: NIST 800-88 defines Clear (overwriting for lower-sensitivity reuse), Purge (degaussing or cryptographic erase for sensitive data), and Destroy (physical destruction — shredding, incineration, disintegration — for the highest assurance of unrecoverability).

q: A technician needs to dispose of an SSD that contained sensitive data. Why is a standard multi-pass overwrite LESS reliable for SSDs than for spinning hard drives?
options: SSDs use wear-leveling that may leave data copies in cells not addressed by a software overwrite
SSDs do not support the ATA Secure Erase command
SSDs store data optically, making magnetic overwriting incompatible
SSDs encrypt data by default, so overwriting is redundant
explanation: SSD wear-leveling distributes writes across flash cells, so a logical overwrite may not reach all physical cells that previously held data. The manufacturer's Secure Erase command or physical destruction is recommended for reliable SSD sanitization.

q: What is the FIRST security step when setting up a new SOHO router?
options: Change the default admin username and password

q: What SOHO router setting should be disabled to reduce the attack surface?

q: A home router default SSID is "Linksys_1234." Why should this be changed?

Default SSIDs broadcast on wrong frequency

A small business owner sets up a new wireless router and wants the strongest available encryption. The router supports WEP, WPA, WPA2, and WPA3. Which should the technician select?
options: WEP, because it is the most universally compatible standard
WPA with TKIP, because TKIP is more secure than AES
WPA2 with TKIP, because TKIP replaced the weaker AES
WPA3, because it provides the strongest current encryption standard
explanation: WPA3 is the current Wi-Fi security standard offering stronger encryption (SAE handshake), protection against offline dictionary attacks, and forward secrecy. WEP is broken; WPA with TKIP has known vulnerabilities; WPA2 with AES is acceptable but WPA3 is preferred when supported.

q: A SOHO router arrives with the SSID set to the ISP's brand name and the admin password set to "admin." Which TWO changes are MOST critical for basic security?
options: Change the default SSID and change the default administrator password
Enable WPS and assign static IPs to all wireless clients
Enable TKIP encryption and disable the DHCP server
Set the wireless channel to auto and enable remote management
explanation: Default SSIDs reveal the router model (aiding attackers in finding known vulnerabilities) and default admin credentials are publicly known. Changing both is the highest-priority first step. WPS should be disabled, not enabled; remote management should also be disabled.

q: A technician configures a SOHO router and wants a separate Wi-Fi network for guests that prevents them from accessing internal file shares and printers. Which feature accomplishes this?
options: MAC address filtering on the primary SSID
Guest network with client isolation enabled
Disabling SSID broadcast on the primary network
Increasing wireless transmit power for guest coverage
explanation: A guest network with client isolation assigns guest devices to a separate network segment and blocks traffic between guest clients and the main LAN. MAC filtering and hidden SSIDs do not create network isolation.

q: A technician recommends disabling Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) on a SOHO router. What is the PRIMARY security reason?
options: WPS prevents dual-band operation on 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz simultaneously
WPS is incompatible with WPA3 and causes connection drops
WPS uses a PIN vulnerable to brute-force attacks due to its split-validation design
WPS broadcasts the network password in plaintext to nearby devices
explanation: The WPS PIN is validated in two halves, reducing the effective keyspace to ~11,000 combinations. Tools like Reaver can brute-force the PIN and derive the WPA passphrase. Disabling WPS eliminates this attack vector.

q: What browser security feature warns users before visiting sites with invalid or expired SSL certificates?

q: What is the purpose of HTTPS (HTTP Secure)?
options: Verifies the website content is appropriate
Encrypts communication between the browser and the web server using TLS

q: What browser security feature prevents websites from being framed in other sites (clickjacking protection)?

q: A user notices websites are tracking browsing habits even after clearing browser history. Which files store session and tracking data in the browser, and what is the correct remediation?
options: Cookies; clear cookies and site data in the browser privacy settings
Cache files; clear the DNS resolver cache using ipconfig /flushdns
Temporary internet files; disable JavaScript in the browser
explanation: Cookies are small text files storing session state and tracking identifiers. Clearing cookies and site data removes tracking information. Browser history and cache are separate; clearing history alone does not remove cookies.

q: A user visits a website and the browser shows "Your connection is not private" with error NET::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID. What does this indicate, and what should the user do?
options: The site uses HTTP; the user should type "https://" manually
The site's SSL/TLS certificate is not trusted by the browser; the user should avoid proceeding unless they can verify the site's legitimacy
The user's connection is too slow to load the certificate; refresh the page
The browser's CRL is outdated; clear cache and retry
explanation: This error means the browser cannot verify the certificate's chain of trust — the certificate may be self-signed, expired, or issued by an untrusted CA. Users should not proceed, as the connection may be intercepted.

q: A company wants to prevent employees from using browsers to visit malicious websites and block inappropriate content categories during work hours. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
explanation: Content filtering (via browser policy, proxy, or DNS filtering) blocks access to URLs or domains based on policy rules. DNS filtering prevents resolution of malicious or policy-violating domains before a connection is established.

q: A user installs a free browser extension claiming to show coupon codes. Shortly after, new toolbars appear, the search engine changes, and ads appear on previously clean pages. What is the MOST likely explanation?
options: The browser needs updating to support the extension
Windows Defender is blocking legitimate browser functionality
The DNS settings were changed by the ISP to show regional ads
The extension is adware or a potentially unwanted program (PUP) that modified browser settings and injects ads
explanation: Browser extensions with broad permissions can modify search engines, inject scripts, and redirect traffic. Free extensions with vague permissions are a common adware delivery vehicle. The extension should be removed and browser settings reset to defaults.

q: Which statement MOST accurately describes what private/incognito browsing mode does and does NOT do?
options: Incognito mode prevents the browser from saving local history, cookies, and form data, but does not hide activity from the network, ISP, or websites visited
Incognito mode encrypts all web traffic, preventing ISP monitoring
Incognito mode blocks all cookies and trackers permanently, even after the session ends
Incognito mode routes traffic through a VPN automatically, masking the user's IP address
explanation: Private/incognito mode creates a temporary session discarded when the window closes — no local history, cookies, or form data are saved on the device. However, the user's IP address, DNS queries, and traffic remain visible to the network administrator, ISP, and websites visited.

The browser cache needs to be cleared
The DNS server address is incorrect
The user's ISP is intercepting search traffic

q: A user is locked out of their Windows account after several failed login attempts, even though they are certain they used the correct password. IT confirms no administrator changed the account. Which condition most likely explains this?
options: Windows Update changed the password policy automatically
An attacker used a brute-force or credential-stuffing attack that triggered the account lockout policy
The user's keyboard is entering incorrect characters
explanation: Account lockout policies trigger after a defined number of failed authentication attempts — the intended defense against brute-force attacks. Being locked out without personally entering a wrong password suggests an attacker was attempting to authenticate.

q: What is the CompTIA recommended FIRST step in the malware removal process?

Back up user data (if possible without spreading malware)

q: After removing malware, what is an important step to prevent reinfection?

q: A user reports that their Android smartphone apps frequently crash shortly after opening. The device has only 200 MB of internal storage remaining. Which action is most likely to resolve the issue?
options: Free up storage space by removing unused apps and cached data
Disable automatic app updates in the Play Store
explanation: Insufficient storage causes apps to crash because they cannot write temporary files or cache data. Clearing cached data and uninstalling unused apps frees space and typically resolves the crashing behavior without data loss.

q: A user's iPhone can connect to cellular data but cannot connect to any Wi-Fi networks, even ones it previously used. Other devices connect to those same networks without issue. Which troubleshooting step should be tried first?
options: Reset Network Settings on the iPhone
explanation: Resetting Network Settings clears saved Wi-Fi passwords, VPN configurations, and cellular settings, resolving many Wi-Fi connectivity problems caused by corrupted network configuration. This is the correct first step when only one device is affected.

q: A user's Android phone battery drains completely within three hours of a full charge with minimal use. The phone is two years old and battery life recently degraded sharply. Which is the most likely cause?
options: Screen resolution is set too high
The battery has chemically degraded and needs replacement
explanation: Lithium-ion batteries degrade over charge cycles and typically show significant capacity loss after 18–24 months of heavy use. A sudden dramatic reduction in battery life in an older device most often indicates a worn battery requiring replacement.

q: A user reports that their phone battery drains very quickly and the device is warm even when idle. What could this indicate?
options: Malware or a rogue app running in the background consuming resources

q: A mobile device is missing from a user desk. What MDM action should be taken immediately?
options: Remotely lock and potentially wipe the device using MDM software

q: What security risk does an unpatched mobile OS pose?
options: Known vulnerabilities remain exploitable by attackers

q: What should a user do if they receive an unsolicited MFA (multi-factor authentication) request they did not initiate?
options: Approve it since it might be a glitch
Call the app support line listed in the MFA message
Deny it and immediately change the account password — credentials may be compromised

q: A user accidentally installs an app that now shows fake virus warnings and demands they call a number. What type of attack is this?

Prevent apps from using the internet

q: A phone starts sending text messages to contacts without user knowledge. What does this indicate?
options: The phone's OS performed an automatic update that installed system apps
The phone has been rooted and malicious apps were sideloaded or installed via exploit
The Google Play Store pushed mandatory enterprise apps
The SIM card was replaced with a different carrier's card
explanation: Rooting removes the security sandbox that prevents unauthorized software installation. Attackers who gain root access or users who sideload APKs from untrusted sources can install malware requesting sensitive permissions without the user's knowledge.

q: An employee's corporate email account was accessed from a foreign country while they were at home. IT confirms no authorized remote session was active. Which is the most appropriate immediate response?
options: Wipe the employee's mobile device remotely
Block all international traffic at the firewall
Revoke and reset the employee's credentials and enable multi-factor authentication
explanation: Unauthorized account access from an unknown location strongly indicates credential theft. Immediately revoking and resetting credentials stops the intrusion, and enabling MFA prevents reuse of the stolen password. Remote wipe may be warranted later but does not address the compromised credentials.

q: A user's mobile data usage is three times higher than normal this month despite no change in habits. The phone has no new recognizable apps. Which security concern does this most likely indicate?
options: The carrier is double-billing for data
Automatic OS updates consumed the extra data
Syncing contacts to the cloud caused the spike
Malware is transmitting data in the background
explanation: Unexpected sustained spikes in mobile data with no obvious user-initiated cause are a classic indicator of malware silently exfiltrating data, receiving commands, or participating in a botnet. The device should be scanned, suspicious apps removed, and credentials changed.

q: [BONUS — Beyond A+ Scope] What document describes the steps to restore IT services after an outage or disaster?

q: What is the purpose of a change management process?

Block all changes to production systems

q: Who typically approves changes in a formal change management process?

q: What is a "change freeze" in IT operations?
options: A period where no changes are allowed, typically around critical business periods

q: What document must be completed before a change is implemented in a formal change management process?
options: Change request (CR) including scope, risk, and rollback plan

q: Before upgrading firmware on a core network switch, a technician documents the current firmware version and tests the upgrade in a lab environment. Which change management practice does this represent?
explanation: Testing changes in a sandbox before applying them to production prevents outages from untested updates. Documenting the current state supports the rollback plan, which allows reverting if the change causes problems.

q: A change request to upgrade a payroll server is evaluated by a cross-functional group including security, operations, and business stakeholders who collectively approve or deny it. What is this group called?
explanation: The Change Advisory Board (CAB) evaluates, approves, or rejects proposed IT changes, ensuring they are assessed for risk, business impact, and scheduling conflicts before implementation.

q: During a planned server migration, the technician migrates additional servers not included in the original approved change request without submitting an updated request. Which change management problem does this represent?
explanation: Scope creep occurs when a change expands beyond what was originally approved without going through the formal change management process, bypassing risk assessment and approval controls.

q: After a software update is applied to production workstations, several critical business applications fail. The technician consults the change documentation and reverses the update successfully. Which change management artifact made the rollback possible?
options: Rollback plan documented in the change request
explanation: A well-written change request includes a rollback plan specifying how to revert the change if it causes problems. Without this documentation, reverting a failed change is slower and riskier.

q: A technician applies a configuration change to a production firewall during approved maintenance hours. Which step should occur immediately after the change is implemented?
options: Submit the change request for CAB approval
Perform verification testing and update the change log
Archive the old firewall and order a replacement
Notify the ISP of the configuration change
explanation: Post-implementation steps include verifying the change worked as expected, confirming no unintended side effects occurred, and updating the change log to maintain an accurate record of the production environment's configuration.

q: What is the purpose of a lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedure?

q: What type of fire suppression system uses an inert gas that does not damage electronic equipment?

q: A technician is about to service a rack-mounted UPS. What precaution is most important?
options: Treat it as energized — UPS units contain large batteries that can deliver dangerous current

q: A technician is about to replace RAM inside a desktop computer. Which precaution is most important to prevent electrostatic discharge (ESD) damage?
options: Work in a room with high humidity to dissipate static
Use rubber-soled shoes and avoid touching metal surfaces
Wear an anti-static wrist strap connected to the chassis ground
Blow compressed air on the RAM slots before installing
explanation: An anti-static wrist strap continuously drains static charge from the technician to ground, preventing ESD damage to sensitive components. This is the primary and most reliable ESD precaution when handling computer hardware.

q: A technician needs to safely dispose of a cleaning chemical used during server maintenance. Which document provides safe handling, storage, disposal, and hazard information?
explanation: Safety Data Sheets (SDS), formerly called MSDS, are standardized documents required by OSHA that provide hazard information, exposure limits, first aid measures, and proper disposal procedures for chemicals.

q: A fire breaks out near a rack of live server equipment. Which type of fire suppression is appropriate?
options: CO2 or clean agent (halon substitute) suppression system
Dry powder extinguisher applied directly to the equipment

q: A company wants to reduce energy consumption from desktop workstations left running overnight. Which power management configuration is most effective?

Upgrade all hard drives to SSDs
explanation: Configuring workstations to hibernate or power off after idle periods dramatically reduces power consumption during unattended hours. Screen savers do not reduce power draw and may increase GPU load.

q: An organization is replacing 50 older laptops and wants to dispose of them responsibly. Which is the correct method?
options: Place them in general office waste recycling bins
Store them indefinitely in a storage room
Disassemble them and dispose of components in separate trash bags
Send them to a certified e-waste recycler or follow local electronic disposal regulations

q: A server room experiences intermittent hardware failures. Temperature monitoring shows 85°F (29°C) during peak hours. What environmental control should be implemented?
options: Increase airflow and cooling capacity through the HVAC system
Install additional UPS units to stabilize power
Replace all spinning drives with SSDs
Add more RAM to reduce processing load
explanation: Servers are designed to operate at 64–80°F (18–27°C). Sustained temperatures above this range cause thermal throttling, component degradation, and hardware failures. Improving HVAC capacity directly addresses the root cause.

q: A used printer toner cartridge needs to be disposed of. Which method is correct?
options: Empty the toner into a trash can and recycle the shell
Return the cartridge through a manufacturer recycling program or certified toner recycler
Rinse the cartridge with water and place it in plastic recycling
Dispose of the cartridge in general office waste
explanation: Toner is a chemically complex powder that should not be released into general waste or the environment. Manufacturer take-back programs and certified recyclers handle toner cartridges safely.

q: Which program certifies that computer equipment meets specific energy efficiency standards set by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency?
explanation: ENERGY STAR is the EPA's voluntary certification program for computers, monitors, and other devices meeting defined energy efficiency benchmarks. RoHS restricts hazardous substances; WEEE governs e-waste in Europe; ISO 14001 is an environmental management standard.

q: A user asks a technician to install a single-license application on five workstations because the company purchased only one license. Which issue does this create?

q: A company receives software at no cost with permission to use, modify, and redistribute the source code under specific terms. Which license type applies?
explanation: Open source licenses (GPL, MIT, Apache) grant users the right to use, view, modify, and redistribute source code under specific conditions. OEM licenses are tied to hardware; volume licenses cover multiple installations; retail licenses are single-user commercial licenses.

q: An employee uses a company laptop and network storage to run a personal side business during work hours. Which policy does this most directly violate?
explanation: An AUP defines what company resources may be used for. Running a personal business on company equipment and storage is a typical AUP violation, using company resources for unauthorized personal gain.

q: A company doing business with EU customers must comply with regulations governing personal data collection, storage, and the right to erasure. Which regulation primarily governs these requirements?
explanation: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is the EU's comprehensive data privacy law granting EU residents rights over their personal data, including access, correction, and deletion. Organizations handling EU residents' data must comply regardless of where they are based.

Escalate to a manager without speaking to the customer

options: Tell them to figure it out

Tell them to call the manufacturer

q: A technician is resolving an issue for a user when their personal cell phone rings. What is the most professional response?

Let the call go to voicemail and continue giving the user full attention
Ask the user to pause while you take the call
Check the caller ID and decide whether to answer
explanation: Letting calls go to voicemail while with a customer demonstrates respect and ensures the user feels heard. Interrupting a customer's explanation for a personal call is unprofessional and undermines trust.

q: A customer is extremely frustrated and begins raising their voice while describing a recurring problem. Which is the most appropriate technician response?
options: Match the customer's tone to demonstrate urgency
Inform the customer you will not help them until they calm down
Remain calm, acknowledge the frustration, and focus on resolving the issue
Transfer the customer to a supervisor immediately
explanation: Staying calm and showing empathy de-escalates tense situations. Acknowledging frustration validates the customer's experience without becoming defensive, which is the foundation of professional customer service.

q: After resolving a workstation issue, which action should the technician take before closing the ticket?
options: Reimage the workstation as a precaution
Submit a change request for the work performed
Follow up with the user to confirm the issue is resolved and they are satisfied
explanation: Following up confirms the fix worked from the user's perspective and demonstrates professional closure. It also provides an opportunity to catch any related issues the user may not have initially reported.

q: A technician is explaining a two-day laptop repair timeline to a user who asks technical questions about the diagnostic process. Which communication approach is most appropriate?
options: Use plain language and avoid excessive jargon so the user understands the situation
Avoid answering technical questions to save time
Use precise technical terminology to demonstrate expertise
Redirect all technical questions to the help desk manager
explanation: Avoiding jargon ensures the customer understands what is happening with their equipment and the timeline, building confidence and reducing anxiety. Technicians should adapt their communication style to the audience's technical level.

q: A user mentions during a support call that they are experiencing personal problems affecting their work. Which is the most appropriate response?
options: Offer personal advice and spend time discussing their situation
Express brief, genuine sympathy and redirect the conversation to the technical issue
Ignore the comment and continue troubleshooting
Document the personal information in the support ticket
explanation: A brief empathetic acknowledgment is appropriate and human, but the technician should redirect to the technical issue to maintain professionalism and productivity. Personal discussions in support contexts and documenting personal matters in tickets are inappropriate.

q: A company maintains a spreadsheet listing every device, its serial number, assigned user, purchase date, and warranty expiration. Which type of documentation is this?
explanation: An asset inventory tracks hardware and software assets including identifying information, assignment, and lifecycle data. It supports auditing, warranty management, and security compliance.

options: The AI's processing speed is too slow

AI bias from training data that reflects historical hiring discrimination

explanation: AI bias occurs when the model's training data reflects historical human biases — such as discriminatory hiring patterns — and the model learns to replicate those patterns. The AI does not intentionally discriminate; it produces outputs that mirror patterns in its training data.

q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between a full backup and a differential backup?
options: A full backup copies only changed files; a differential copies all files
A full backup is performed weekly; a differential daily by definition
A full backup copies all selected data; a differential copies all data changed since the last full backup
A differential backup requires no baseline and is independent of other backups
explanation: A full backup copies all selected data regardless of changes. A differential backup copies all data changed since the last full backup, growing larger each day until the next full backup. This differs from incremental backups, which only copy data changed since the last backup of any type.
